meta.title: The Second Turn
meta.skill_frame: Literary text: track two characters and read what one quiet example teaches.

reader.who: Older students who read at about a fourth-grade level.
reader.why_this_level: Measured FK 5.5 over the three parts (109 words at FK 5.6, 113 words at FK 5.4, 100 words at FK 5.5). The load is two characters whose habits change in opposite directions, and a quiet example the reader has to read as the cause.
reader.tone: Adult subject. Plain sentences. The lesson must not make the reader feel small.

source.attribution: Original text drafted for literary_text 4.1, Band 4.1, sequence 1. No external work.
source.text_status: Drafted for the band, accepted on spot check.
source.survey: A repair shop where both people change in opposite directions, so the reader holds two arcs at once.
source.avoided: No shop name, street, town, or price. No claim about what the shop paid the helper.

session.difficulty_basis: two characters whose habits change in opposite directions, and a quiet example the reader has to read as the cause

script_overrides.near_copy_2: Say it in your own words. One sentence is enough.

passage.part_1: The owner of the repair shop checks every wheel the same way, and he has done it that way for twenty years. He spins the wheel once to hear the bearing, then spins it again with the flat of his hand on the rim. The new helper works faster than that and sees no point in the second spin. He looks a wheel over, hangs it back on the rack, and calls the next job from the doorway. That spring the shop took in more bikes than it had racks for, and the owner stopped watching the helper at all. The helper stopped asking to be watched as well.
passage.part_2: On a wet Friday a courier brought back a wheel the helper had fitted on Monday. The rim had worked loose, and the brake block had rubbed the tyre flat on one side. The owner said nothing to the courier and nothing to the helper. He refunded the charge for the week, ordered a new rim from the supplier, and fitted it himself while the shop stayed open. The helper watched from the bench and did not get up to help. When the courier left, the owner went back to his own bench and started the next job on the rack without a word. He did not ask who had fitted the wheel.
passage.part_3: By the next month the helper spun every wheel twice, and the owner had stopped. Orders were behind, so he was fitting wheels without the second spin, and his bench was the one that gave trouble. The owner was out front, taking in three more bikes and promising all of them for Friday. On a Thursday the helper found a loose nut on a wheel the owner had signed off. He spun that wheel twice, took it off the bike, and made the nut tight. Then he hung the wheel on the rack and said nothing about it to anyone.

items.prompt: How does the owner check a wheel before it leaves his bench?

tutor_only.confirm: Right. He spins it twice, and the second spin is by hand.
tutor_only.correct_reason: The sentence about his check says he spins the wheel once to hear the bearing, then again with his hand flat on the rim.
tutor_only.tell: The owner spins each wheel twice. The first spin listens to the bearing. The second feels the rim by hand.
help: The sentence about the wheel check says what he does before the wheel leaves.
There are two spins, and the second one uses his hand.
tutor_only.core_idea: He spins the wheel twice, once to hear the bearing and once by hand on the rim.
accept_ideas: once to hear the bearing and again by hand
he turns it twice by hand
tutor_only.normalize: Ignore case, punctuation, and minor spelling. Accept a meaning-preserving paraphrase.

if_they_say.when: the student says he looks the wheel over
if_they_say.ask: The passage gives him two steps with each wheel. What are they?

items.prompt: Why did the owner stop watching the helper at all that spring?

tutor_only.confirm: Yes. The shop took in more bikes than it had racks for.
tutor_only.correct_reason: The sentence about that spring says the shop took in more bikes than it had racks for, and the owner stopped watching. The passage gives no reason about trusting the helper.
tutor_only.tell: The shop filled with bikes that spring. The owner was too busy to watch the helper work.
help: The sentence about that spring gives the reason the watching stopped.
It is about how many bikes the shop took in.
tutor_only.core_idea: The shop had more bikes than racks, so the owner was too busy.
accept_ideas: there were more bikes than racks
he had more work than he could handle
not_required: how long the owner had run the shop
tutor_only.normalize: Ignore case, punctuation, and minor spelling. Accept a meaning-preserving paraphrase.

if_they_say.when: the student says the owner trusted the helper or thought he could handle the work
if_they_say.ask: The passage does not say the owner trusted him. What changed in the shop that spring?

if_they_say.when: the student says the helper was fast or good at his job
if_they_say.ask: Speed is what the helper did, not why the watching stopped. What changed in the shop?

items.prompt: The owner refunded the charge and fitted the new rim himself. What did that show about how he treated the helper's mistake?

tutor_only.confirm: Right. He treated it as his own problem, not the helper's.
tutor_only.correct_reason: The sentence about the refund says who paid and who did the work, and the passage says he said nothing to the helper.
tutor_only.tell: He paid the customer back and did the work himself. The helper was never named for it.
help: The sentence about the refund says who paid and who did the work.
The owner did both, and he said nothing to the helper.
tutor_only.core_idea: He took the mistake on himself and fixed it without blaming the helper.
accept_ideas: he fixed it himself instead of blaming the helper
he treated it as his own job
tutor_only.normalize: Ignore case, punctuation, and minor spelling. Accept a meaning-preserving paraphrase.

if_they_say.when: the student says he did not notice the mistake
if_they_say.ask: He brought the wheel back to his own bench and fitted a new rim. Why do that?

items.prompt: By the end the helper checks every wheel twice and the owner does not. What does the story show caused that?

tutor_only.confirm: Yes. One learned the habit from the other, and the other lost his own.
tutor_only.correct_reason: The owner fitted the bad wheel himself without a word, and the helper copied that way with the loose nut.
tutor_only.tell: The helper learned from watching the owner fix the bad wheel. The owner lost his check when orders piled up.
help: Read what the owner did with the returned wheel, then what the helper did the next month.
One of them learned a habit, and the other one lost it.
tutor_only.core_idea: The owner's example taught the helper, and the owner dropped his own check when work piled up.
accept_ideas: the owner showed him how to fix a mistake quietly
the owner stopped because he was behind
not_required: how many bikes the shop repaired that month
tutor_only.normalize: Ignore case, punctuation, and minor spelling. Accept a meaning-preserving paraphrase.

if_they_say.when: the student says the helper was told to check twice
if_they_say.ask: Nothing shows the owner telling him. What did the helper see the owner do?

items.prompt: The helper found the owner's loose nut and said nothing about it. What does that show about what he had learned?

tutor_only.confirm: Right. He had learned to fix a mistake quietly, the way the owner did.
tutor_only.correct_reason: He made the nut tight, put the wheel back, and said nothing. That is what the owner did with the returned wheel.
tutor_only.tell: He made the nut tight and said nothing. That is what the owner did with his wheel in the first week.
help: Compare what the helper did with the nut with what the owner did about the bad wheel.
Both of them fixed a mistake without naming it.
tutor_only.core_idea: He had learned to fix a mistake quietly, the way the owner did.
accept_ideas: he copied the owner's way of fixing mistakes
he fixed it without blaming anyone
he learned from the owner's example
not_required: what the owner said to the courier
tutor_only.normalize: Ignore case, punctuation, and minor spelling. Accept a meaning-preserving paraphrase.

if_they_say.when: the student says he was afraid of the owner
if_they_say.ask: The passage shows no fear. What did the owner do when he found the bad wheel?
